top_stories.title: 'Will Pakistan recognise Israel?' Viral clip captures journalist confronting foreign minister Ishaq Dar - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ishaq Dar**, Pakistan's deputy prime minister and foreign minister, and **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, engaged in a video exchange that reignited debate about Pakistan potentially recognizing Israel.  Dar reiterated Pakistan's stance that it would not alter its position on the matter unless there was significant progress towards an independent Palestinian state. He emphasized Pakistan's commitment to the Palestinian cause and stressed that any shift in policy regarding Israel would only occur after a Palestinian state is established. Despite public speculation, Pakistan has maintained its official position against recognizing Israel.  Pakistan continues to play a prominent role in diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions between the United States and Iran.

top_stories.title: Claims of being vishwaguru but can't conduct single exam: Rahul's dig at PM - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for the delayed CUET-UG 2026 examination, alleging that the government has destroyed the education system.  He accused **Modi** of being unable to conduct even a single examination properly despite claiming to be a "vishwaguru." **Gandhi** stated that this failure is impacting millions of students and will hold **Modi** accountable for his actions.

top_stories.title: ‘Kidnapping for ransom’ triable by ATC, Peshawar High Court declares - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Peshawar High Court** ruled that a case of kidnapping for ransom, included in the Anti-Terrorism Act's Schedule, is triable by an anti-terrorism court. The court rejected pleas from four accused in the Dr Warda Mushtaq murder case seeking to transfer their case to an ordinary court.  The court upheld an order from the ATC Hazara region that allowed for the trial of the accused under Section 365-A (kidnapping for ransom) of the Pakistan Penal Code, despite initial inclusion of the charge under Section 7 of the ATA. The court emphasized that kidnapping for ransom is a serious offense affecting public safety and societal order, justifying its inclusion in the Anti-Terrorism Act's jurisdiction.

top_stories.title: Eighteen people killed in Afghanistan truck crash, including 10 children | Afghanistan | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: An overturned truck in eastern Afghanistan killed 18 people, including 10 children, on Saturday. **Abdul Malik Niazay**, spokesperson for the governor of Laghman province, said the vehicle was carrying Afghan families returning from Pakistan. The accident occurred along a road between Jalalabad and Kabul.  **Pakistan's** tough stance on Afghan migrants has led to an increase in family travel by truck, contributing to these tragic incidents.

top_stories.title: Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund announces launch of its SIF platform MPOWER - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Mahindra Manulife Investment Management** launched **MPOWER SIF**, a new investment solution designed to meet the evolving needs of investors seeking greater flexibility and diverse risk-return outcomes. The fund house aims to provide clients with an experience tailored to their aspirations while adhering to consistent and meaningful investment outcomes.  The launch is driven by the belief that this platform, utilizing a wider investment toolkit, will enable more agile portfolio construction strategies.

top_stories.title: UK will use AI to screen migrants ‘posing as minors’ - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The UK Home Office** will deploy an artificial intelligence age estimation tool at its borders beginning next year. The software, developed by a private company and tested for accuracy, aims to identify adult migrants attempting to deceive the system by misrepresenting their age. **Human Rights Watch** has criticized the technology as unproven and potentially harmful to vulnerable children who rely on legal protections for asylum seekers.  The government's decision comes amid rising numbers of people crossing the English Channel in small boats seeking asylum.

top_stories.title: Voting ongoing in snap elections in Malta, governing party expected to win | Politics News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: Malta's snap parliamentary election is underway, with voters facing concerns over rising rents and ailing infrastructure. **Robert Abela**, leader of the governing Labour Party, faces a challenge from **Alex Borg** of the Nationalist Party, who hopes to become Malta's youngest-ever prime minister at 30. The election comes amid economic anxieties caused by global market fluctuations and the ongoing Iran war.  The outcome is expected to be announced on Sunday.

top_stories.title: How Charlie Munger’s behavioral lessons apply to today’s market reality - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Charlie Munger's** famous list of "human misjudgment tendencies" is proving relevant in today's market, where higher-for-longer interest rates, liquidity concentration, and emotionally driven retail participation are shaping investor behavior.  Investors are prone to emotional distortions like FOMO and envy, leading to poor portfolio decisions based on short-term trends rather than fundamental value. **Munger** also warns against overconfidence in the face of prolonged market gains and emphasizes the importance of discipline, focusing on long-term fundamentals and avoiding impulsive reactions to news or social pressure.  In essence, success lies in mitigating emotional biases and making informed decisions based on value rather than fleeting trends.

top_stories.title: Greek National Charged Espionage Uk: Greek man appears in court charged over alleged plot to spy on Iranian journalist in London | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ioannis Aidinidis**, a 36-year-old Greek national, was charged with espionage related to alleged surveillance and information gathering activities against an Iranian journalist living in London between 2024 and 2025. The **Metropolitan Police Counter Terrorism Command** led the investigation, which is being prosecuted by the **Crown Prosecution Service**. This case has raised concerns about foreign-linked surveillance operations in Britain, particularly targeting journalists and dissidents.  The case will continue to be closely watched as it progresses through the British court system.

top_stories.title: US, South Korea in talks over commander's remarks that drew sharp criticism from China - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **South Korea** and the **United States** are engaged in discussions following remarks by the commander of **US Forces Korea**, **Xavier Brunson**, who described South Korea as a "dagger in the heart of Asia."  The Chinese embassy in Seoul criticized these comments, calling them hostile and aggressive. The **Blue House** has complained to the US over Brunson's statements, which have been raised previously. While specific details remain unclear, both countries are maintaining communication regarding the issue.
